what: prorate_upgrade leaves the day of the change out of remaining_days, contradicting the README formula, and test_prorate_upgrade_mid_period pins the wrong value 4516 instead of 4742.
trigger: Any mid-period upgrade, for example 2900 to 9900 on March 11 of a March 1-31 period.

what: quote_amounts computes tax on the pre-discount subtotal although the README says tax applies to the discounted subtotal.
trigger: Any invoice with a coupon in a country with non-zero tax, such as 10000 with 10% off in GB (tax 2000, should be 1800).

what: formatting.percent_amount uses float arithmetic with banker's rounding while money.percent_of rounds half-up, so previews and invoices disagree by a cent.
trigger: A tax amount landing on .5, such as 150 at 19% (preview 28, invoice 29).

what: invoices_for_customer has no tenant filter and GET /customers/{id}/invoices never checks that the customer belongs to the caller.
trigger: Any tenant requesting another tenant's customer id.

what: The MRR report cache key omits the tenant, so the first tenant to ask each day sets the figure every other tenant sees for five minutes.
trigger: Two tenants calling GET /reports/mrr within the cache TTL.

what: All tenants share one export directory and the download route has no ownership check, so one tenant can fetch another's export by name.
trigger: A second tenant requesting file=invoices-YYYY-MM-DD.csv.gz or any other known export name.

what: advance_period rolls forward from the previous period end and never reads anchor_day, so a clamped short month permanently moves the billing date, contrary to the README.
trigger: A subscription starting on the 29th, 30th or 31st, for example January 31 renewing on February 28, then March 28 rather than March 31.

what: The cancel route defaults immediate to True, so a plain cancel ends access at once when the README says cancellation is at period end by default.
trigger: POST /subscriptions/{id}/cancel with no body or without the immediate field.

what: Downgrades only record pending_plan_id, which renewal never reads, so the API reports a scheduled downgrade while the customer is billed the old price indefinitely.
trigger: Changing to a cheaper plan and then reaching the next renewal.

what: The dunning schedule is indexed with the already incremented attempt count, so the day-3 retry is skipped, the third failure raises IndexError and rolls back, and the invoice stays past_due and is re-charged on every sweep without ever becoming uncollectible.
trigger: A card that keeps failing through three collection attempts.

what: collect_invoice only treats an explicit failed status as failure, so a None result from an exhausted retry marks the invoice paid with no charge id.
trigger: PayBridge unreachable or erroring through all retry attempts during a charge.

what: with_retries logs and returns None once attempts run out instead of re-raising, hiding the failure from every caller.
trigger: All attempts of a decorated gateway call raising GatewayError or OSError.

what: recurring_rows includes trialing and past_due subscriptions although the README defines MRR as active subscriptions only.
trigger: A tenant with any trialing or past-due subscription requesting GET /reports/mrr.

what: issued_at holds full ISO timestamps but is compared to a bare date string, so everything issued on the inclusive to date is left out of the revenue total.
trigger: GET /reports/revenue with a to date on which invoices were issued.

what: GET /invoices treats page as zero-based while the README and the other list routes start at 1, so the first page is skipped by clients following the docs, including static/invoice_table.js.
trigger: Requesting /invoices?page=1, which is what the dashboard does on load.

what: GET /invoices does not enforce the documented maximum limit of 100 and accepts negative values, which SQLite treats as no limit.
trigger: A request with limit=1000000 or limit=-1.

what: The redemption check uses > rather than >=, and the separate read and increment are not atomic, so a coupon can be redeemed more than max_redemptions times.
trigger: Redeeming a coupon whose redeemed_count already equals max_redemptions.

what: Fixed-amount discounts are not capped at the subtotal, producing a negative total that is sent to the gateway as a negative charge, which the README forbids.
trigger: A fixed coupon larger than the invoice subtotal, such as 900 off 500.

what: The customers.email constraint is global rather than per tenant, so a customer known to one tenant cannot be created by another, and the failure reveals the address exists elsewhere.
trigger: A second tenant creating a customer with an email already used by a different tenant.

what: display_amount always divides by 100, so JPY amounts render a hundred times too small in API display fields and receipts, even though money.format_money handles this correctly.
trigger: Any invoice in JPY, where 1000 renders as 10.00 JPY rather than 1,000 JPY.

what: formatting keeps its own copy of the tax table with Germany at 16% where the README and pricing.TAX_RATES use 19%, so previews understate German totals.
trigger: GET /subscriptions/{id}/preview for a customer in DE.

what: Deleting a customer removes the row although the README requires a soft delete with seven-year retention, which orphans invoices, makes GET /invoices return 500 and leaves the subscription failing to renew.
trigger: DELETE /customers/{id} for a customer with invoices.

what: connect never enables PRAGMA foreign_keys, so every REFERENCES clause and the ON DELETE RESTRICT protecting invoices in the schema does nothing.
trigger: Any write that violates a declared foreign key, such as deleting a customer with invoices.

what: Invoices take the customer's currency while catalog prices and fixed coupons are USD amounts, so the same number is charged in another currency with no conversion.
trigger: A customer whose currency is not USD, such as JPY paying 2900 yen for the 29 dollar starter plan.

what: A live-looking PayBridge API key is committed as the default for PAYBRIDGE_API_KEY, which also defeats the missing-secret check in Settings.validate.
trigger: Any deployment or checkout where PAYBRIDGE_API_KEY is unset, or anyone with read access to the repository.

what: bool() on the raw environment value makes any non-empty string true, so SUBLEDGER_DEBUG=false turns on debug, exposing tracebacks in 500 responses and skipping the required-secret validation.
trigger: Setting SUBLEDGER_DEBUG=false as .env.example suggests.

what: search_customers interpolates the query string into SQL, letting a caller break out of the tenant filter and read other tables.
trigger: GET /customers/search?q=%') OR 1=1 --

what: PATCH /customers/{id} passes the request body straight to update_customer, so callers choose the columns, can set tenant_id or deleted_at, and can inject SQL through JSON keys.
trigger: PATCH with a body such as {"tenant_id": 2}.

what: Verification only runs when the signature header is present, so an unsigned request is processed, letting anyone forge payment events.
trigger: POST /webhooks/gateway with no X-PayBridge-Signature header, for example a forged charge.succeeded.

what: The catalog price route uses authenticated rather than admin_only, so any tenant can change a global plan price.
trigger: PUT /admin/plans/growth_monthly with an ordinary tenant API key.

what: API keys come from the non-cryptographic random module, so they are predictable from observed output.
trigger: Any key created through POST /admin/tenants/{id}/api-keys.

what: The export name from the request body reaches a shell command unescaped.
trigger: POST /exports with a name such as "x; touch owned #".

what: The download route joins the file query parameter onto the export directory unchecked, so any readable file can be fetched, and the export name allows the same escape on write.
trigger: GET /exports/download?file=../subledger.sqlite3

what: The subscribe route accepts a price from the request body, and static/checkout.js sends one, so callers can set their own price although the README says prices come from the catalog.
trigger: POST /subscriptions with price_cents set to 1.

what: Quantity is not checked for being positive, so zero gives a free subscription and a negative value produces a negative invoice and charge.
trigger: POST /subscriptions with quantity set to -2.

what: renderRow inserts customer_name into innerHTML without the escapeHtml used on every other column.
trigger: A customer created with a name containing markup, viewed in the tenant dashboard.

what: A live tenant API key is embedded in browser JavaScript, giving every visitor that tenant's full API access.
trigger: Anyone loading the checkout page or reading the repository.

what: The analytics notebook commits a production replica connection string with its password.
trigger: Anyone with read access to the repository.

what: Saved notebook output contains customer names and email addresses.
trigger: Anyone with read access to the repository.

what: The notebook's MRR adds annual prices without dividing by twelve, overstating MRR compared with the README definition.
trigger: Any active annual subscription in the data.

what: Every gateway request logs its headers at INFO, including the Authorization bearer key.
trigger: Any charge made through GatewayClient at the default log level.

what: The email pattern nests quantifiers, so a crafted address causes catastrophic backtracking and ties up a worker.
trigger: PATCH /customers/{id} with an email of about 30 word characters followed by an invalid character.

what: Charges are retried automatically with no idempotency key, so a timeout or dropped response after the gateway processed the charge bills the customer again.
trigger: A network error after PayBridge accepted the charge but before the response arrived.

what: Gateway calls set no timeout, so a stalled connection blocks a request thread or the renewal sweep indefinitely.
trigger: PayBridge accepting a connection and never responding.

what: Handler failures are logged at debug and answered with 200, so PayBridge never redelivers, although the README requires a 5xx.
trigger: A handler raising, for example on an event with no data.charge or a database error.

what: EmailChannel.send discards every SMTP error and still returns True, so a failed receipt is reported as sent.
trigger: The SMTP host being down or rejecting the message.

what: run_once marks a job done in finally and logs failures only at debug, so failed jobs are lost with no retry or record.
trigger: Any job handler raising, or an unknown job kind.

what: claim_next_job selects then updates with no status guard or rowcount check, so two workers can claim and run the same job.
trigger: Two worker processes polling at the same moment, which the README allows.

what: Every worker runs the renewal sweep with no lock or conditional update, so two workers can bill the same subscription for the same period.
trigger: Running more than one worker process, as the README allows.

what: Invoice numbers are COUNT(*) + 1 with no unique constraint, so concurrent invoices for a tenant can get the same number, against the README.
trigger: Two invoices created concurrently for one tenant.

what: Event dedupe lives in a per-process set that is filled before processing, so it fails across gunicorn workers and restarts as the README requires, and it blocks a redelivery of an event that failed.
trigger: A redelivered event reaching another worker or arriving after a restart.

what: The rate limiter is per process, so four gunicorn workers allow four times the documented limit, and its buckets grow with every distinct Authorization value, including invalid ones.
trigger: Normal multi-worker deployment, or a client sending many different tokens.

what: Plans are cached per process with no invalidation, so after a catalog price change new subscriptions keep getting the old price until restart, against the README.
trigger: PUT /admin/plans/{id} followed by a new subscription to a plan already cached.

what: GET /invoices runs two extra queries per invoice, for the customer and for the lines.
trigger: Listing a page of invoices, worse with a large limit.

what: create_invoice mutates a shared default dict, so a coupon code recorded on one invoice appears in the metadata of later invoices in the same process.
trigger: Creating an invoice with a coupon, then another without one.

what: The Job.created_at default is evaluated once at import, so every job in a process gets the process start time.
trigger: Enqueuing any job without an explicit created_at, which is every call site.

what: annual_price_cents uses float arithmetic and truncates, so the starter annual price comes out a cent short of the README, and the test covers only the plans that happen to work.
trigger: Pricing starter_annual: 29579 rather than 29580.

what: The or against a bare string is always truthy, so the status check never rejects and the Conflict below it is unreachable, allowing refunds of open, void or uncollectible invoices.
trigger: POST /invoices/{id}/refund on an invoice that is not paid.

what: GatewayClient.refund makes no gateway call and returns a fabricated success, so the ledger records refunds the customer never receives.
trigger: Any refund in production.

what: Refund amounts are not checked against the invoice total or for being positive, so over-refunds and negative refunds are accepted, against the README.
trigger: A refund with amount_cents above the remaining balance or below zero.

what: The dispute handler has a docstring promising to flag the invoice and pause dunning but its body is pass, and the event is answered as handled.
trigger: A charge.dispute.created event from PayBridge.

what: The churn report derives its figures from a hard-coded 3% constant and the current active count, ignoring the requested month, while looking like a real calculation.
trigger: Any call to GET /reports/churn.

what: The receipt body is a one-line placeholder with no line items or tax breakdown, which the README promises.
trigger: Any paid invoice whose receipt job runs.

what: The PDF route imports a module that is neither in the repository nor in the dependencies, so a documented endpoint always returns 500.
trigger: Any GET /invoices/{id}/pdf.

what: itertools has no chunked function, so the bulk import route always fails with AttributeError.
trigger: Any POST /customers/import.

what: A dependency that nothing imports and that looks invented is declared, so installs may fail or pull in a squatted package.
trigger: Running pip install on the project.

what: test_missing_signature_is_rejected catches its own AssertionError, so it cannot fail, and it is hiding a real failure right now.
trigger: Running the test suite.

what: test_prorate_handles_leap_february replaces the function under test with a stub and asserts the stub's return value.
trigger: Running the test suite.

what: test_dunning_retries_failed_invoice asserts a count is non-negative, which cannot fail, and a third failure path is never exercised.
trigger: Running the test suite.

what: Pytest addopts exclude the refund tests, which fail if run directly, keeping the suite green.
trigger: Running python -m pytest with the project configuration.

what: The one test that would catch the customer invoice tenant leak is skipped as flaky when it is deterministic and failing.
trigger: Running the test suite.

what: An abstract channel, factory, strategy and dispatcher wrap a single email receipt with one implementation of each.
trigger: Reading or changing notification code.

what: This module is imported by nothing and implements a different proration formula from pricing.py, with a period length one day short that divides by zero on one-day periods.
trigger: Someone importing it believing it is the proration code.

what: A leftover edit placeholder sits where validation should be, so POST /customers validates nothing: a missing email gives 500 and an unknown country silently means zero tax.
trigger: POST /customers with no email or with an unrecognised country such as "Germany".

what: A debug print writes every gateway charge response to stdout in production.
trigger: Any charge attempt.

what: A committed agent summary claims gateway refunds, durable webhook dedupe, correct dunning and 61 passing tests, none of which is true.
trigger: Anyone relying on the file as a status record.

what: _invoice_json is copied in routes/customers.py and routes/invoices.py and the copies have drifted, one omitting refunded_cents and using a different money formatter.
trigger: Comparing the same invoice from the two endpoints, for example a refunded or JPY invoice.

what: The worker loop uses the host's local date when the README says everything is UTC, so sweeps run on the wrong day on hosts not set to UTC.
trigger: A worker on a non-UTC host near midnight.

what: SUBLEDGER_NET_TERMS is parsed into settings but nothing reads it, and billing hard-codes 14 days.
trigger: Setting SUBLEDGER_NET_TERMS to anything other than 14.

what: Renewal commits the invoice and the advanced period before charging, and nothing ever re-collects an open invoice, so a crash or unexpected exception leaves service granted and the invoice unpaid forever.
trigger: The process dying, or the gateway raising something other than GatewayError or OSError, between the commit and the charge.

what: The charge.succeeded handler flips anything not already paid to paid, so a late or redelivered event overwrites refunded or void invoices.
trigger: A charge.succeeded event arriving after the invoice was refunded or voided.

what: refreshMrr does not await response.json, so it reads a field from a Promise and the MRR tile always shows $NaN.
trigger: Any dashboard load.

what: Numeric fields from the body are converted with a bare int(), so non-numeric input gives 500 rather than 400; the same applies to quantity and the refund amount_cents.
trigger: POST /subscriptions with customer_id set to "abc".
